Evidence mode: handoff only. Give a supported first answer now. Set recover to true only if seeing the complete history would help resolve missing evidence; otherwise false. At most one source followup will be served after this answer is saved.

QUESTION
Replace the exact calibration only for this hypothetical: the gateway is ahead by one common unknown offset in the closed interval [2,4] seconds. Which unique samples are guaranteed to pass, guaranteed to fail, or unresolved under the two-second requirement? Is it possible that all three pass?

EVIDENCE
STATUS
At Day 12, two of three unique samples pass delivery within two seconds: S and T each take 1 second; U takes 3 seconds and fails. Pass rate is 2/3 (66.7%); lateness is 1/3 (33.3%). U-retry is U’s transmission alias, not another sample. Dashboard clock correction and identity grouping remain unreleased (C09).

EVIDENCE
C03–C05 give acquisition/gateway/database timestamps: S 100/104/111; T 100.5/104.5/111; U 102/108/113. C07 establishes gateway = reference +3 throughout arrivals, replacing the withdrawn +1 guess, with no current uncertainty. Corrected first arrivals are 101, 101.5, 105. Delivery means gateway arrival, not database insertion; equality at two seconds passes. Insertion follows arrival by 10, 9.5, 8 seconds respectively. C08 confirms the complete three-sample catalogue and first-arrival observations. C06’s four late rows describe the uncorrected display, not confirmed unique failures. Shared insertion batching and preview styling supply no new arrival evidence.

NEXT
Use preserved rows and calibration now; display release is unnecessary for calculation. For a hypothetical closed offset interval [a,b], delay lies in [g−acquisition−b, g−acquisition−a]; the upper endpoint is worst-case delay. For S/T, guaranteed pass requires a≥2, guaranteed failure b<2; for U, a≥4 or b<4 respectively. Otherwise classification is indeterminate (C10). Retain the exact current offset unless explicitly changed. Recover definitions and scope from C01, C11–C12; do not extrapolate to unseen samples or days.
